drills.hint: jātā hūn — stem जा + ता (m.) + auxiliary हूँ for 'I'
khātī hai — feminine subject takes -ती, auxiliary है
karte hain — plural/respect takes -ते and हैं
jāūngā — future adds -ऊँगा; -गी for feminine

drills.q: 'I ate' (using ने, masculine speaker) in Hindi?
drills.hint: mainne khāyā — transitive past: subject takes ने, verb is perfective खाया
khā rahā hūn — continuous uses stem + रहा/रही + auxiliary
pānī — masculine noun
dost — same word for male or female friend
baṛā — becomes बड़ी for feminine nouns
kal — context decides past or future
dhanyavād — शुक्रिया is a common alternative

drills.q: Which postposition marks 'in the house': घर ___ ?
drills.hint: men — 'in/inside'; पर would mean 'on'

drills.q: The respectful word for 'you' in Hindi?
drills.hint: āp — takes plural verb; तुम is familiar, तू is intimate

drills.q: Feminine form of the adjective अच्छा (good)?
drills.hint: acchī — -आ adjectives change -आ to -ई for feminine

drills.q: Oblique form of लड़का before a postposition (e.g. ___ को)?
drills.hint: laṛke — masculine -आ nouns shift to -ए in the oblique
sāt — छह is six, आठ is eight
sau — हज़ार is thousand
āp kaise hain? — कैसी हैं when addressing a woman
yah kitne kā hai? — key shopping question
mujhe samajh nahīn āyā — literally 'to me understanding did not come'
